findings.text: follow-on: seed_facility_roots returns result["processed"], the number of canonical root rows it UNWINDs (for jt-60sa, the configured roots), not the number newly created. The --add-roots branch prints `Added {seeded} new root path(s) from config`, so after this change it always reports every configured root as new, even when none was created; the retired seed_missing_roots returned only the missing count. Reporting-only, not a data defect, but the message no longer distinguishes 'added' from 'all present'.

follow-on: the create-only semantics are pinned by a fake session that emulates Neo4j's MERGE/ON CREATE SET and by a query-text regex, not by a live-graph assertion. The emulation is faithful to the two Cypher forms the method emits and the query-form test pins the exact clause, but a `-m graph` test that MERGEs an existing id with ON CREATE SET and reads the unchanged properties back would exercise the database's own semantics rather than a local model of them. This mirrors the earlier reset-pin node's finding that the pin stops at the forwarding boundary.

The focused gate `tests/graph/test_create_nodes_create_only.py tests/discovery/test_seed_existing_roots.py` reran green (7 passed, EXIT=0). justifications.fit: two conventional commits — `feat(discovery): make root seeding create-only` and `docs(evidence): record create-only root seeding` — each with a body stating what changed and why; no AI attribution, no plan/sprint/ticket identifier or phase name in subjects, bodies, symbol names, filenames or comments; the new test files are named for the capability (create_nodes create-only, seed existing roots).
justifications.goal_fidelity: the plan's seed-fix node is implemented exactly as written: create_only off by default via ON CREATE SET, relationship creation unchanged, canonical and alias seed rows written with it, seed_missing_roots retired with exports removed from both __init__.py, --add-roots calling seed_facility_roots(facility), create_child_paths deleted, and both tests present as specified.
